---
title: "Quiz · Portability"
---

A short knowledge check. Answers are hidden behind callouts so you can
self-grade after answering.

## 1. Does Pico Engine 1.6 complete Pico portability?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
No. It provides an essential **prerequisite** (cryptographic identity,
pairwise relationships, encrypted communication). The engine's base URL still
remains part of the did:webvh, so identity cannot yet move unchanged between
engines.
:::

## 2. Name two of the four remaining-work areas.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Full identity portability, verifiable credentials, key management, and
identity-aware authorization.
:::

## 3. What is the design objective for key management?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Losing a cryptographic key should not mean losing the Pico. Keys should move
toward OS key vaults, hardware-backed storage, secure enclaves, or external
KMS, with key rotation and recovery developed.
:::

## 4. Why must the Open Engineering identifier stay distinct from the runtime DID?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
They answer different questions: the OE identifier says "what Open
Engineering element is this?" while the did:webvh says "which cryptographic
Pico is this?" and the did:peer says "which private relationship is this?"
Keeping them separate supports portability — the semantic identity should
survive an engine move even when the runtime DID changes.
:::
